questions.question: Which three methods form the core of the Iterator interface?
questions.explanation: hasNext() checks for another element, next() returns it and moves the cursor, and remove() deletes the last element returned.

questions.question: Where does an iterator's cursor sit?
options: In the gap between two elements
At the end of the collection
questions.explanation: The cursor starts before the first element. Each next() jumps over one element and returns it, leaving the cursor in the next gap.

questions.question: What does this print? List<String> l = new ArrayList<>(List.of("a", "b", "c")); Iterator<String> it = l.iterator(); it.next(); it.remove(); System.out.println(it.next() + l);
questions.explanation: remove() deletes a, the element just returned. The cursor stays in its gap, so the next call returns b, and the list is [b, c].

questions.question: A loop does for (String s : list) { if (s.isEmpty()) list.remove(s); } on an ArrayList and crashes. What is the cause?
options: isEmpty() cannot be called on list elements
The list changed its modCount outside the hidden iterator, so next() throws
questions.explanation: The fail-fast iterator sees that modCount no longer matches its expected count and throws ConcurrentModificationException.

questions.question: Why does this throw IllegalStateException? Iterator<String> it = list.iterator(); it.remove();
options: remove() was called before any next(), so there is no element to remove
The list must be a LinkedList
questions.explanation: remove() deletes the element last returned by next(). With no next() call yet, or after a second remove(), it throws IllegalStateException.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe way to remove matching items from an ArrayList while walking it?
options: list.add(x) and then list.remove(x) inside for-each
questions.explanation: removeIf walks and removes inside the list itself. Using the iterator's own remove() is also safe.

questions.question: What does this print? Iterator<Integer> it = List.of(7).iterator(); it.next(); System.out.println(it.hasNext());
questions.explanation: After the single element is returned, no element lies ahead, so hasNext() returns false. Only a further next() would throw.

questions.question: Which feature does ListIterator add that a plain Iterator does not have?
questions.explanation: ListIterator works only on lists and adds hasPrevious, previous, nextIndex, previousIndex, set and add.

questions.question: What does this print? List<Integer> l = new ArrayList<>(List.of(1, 2)); ListIterator<Integer> it = l.listIterator(); it.next(); it.set(9); System.out.println(l);
questions.explanation: set replaces the element last returned by next(), which was 1, so the list becomes [9, 2].

questions.question: What must a class implement so its objects can be used in a for-each loop?
questions.explanation: The for-each loop calls iterator() on an Iterable. A class only needs to implement Iterable and return an Iterator.
